To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

obesity and high-calorie diets are associated with increased coagulation, decreased fibrinolysis, platelet reactivity and endothelial function and that a mediterranean-like diet with its high content of olive oil and omega 3 fatty acids, polyphenols and moderate alcohol consumption is associated with a beneficial effect on haemostatic and thrombotic risk.
a mediterranean type of diet with high content of unsaturated fatty acids, polyphenols and alcohol is beneficial for the haemostasis and thrombotic risk.
a healthy diet rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and fish is associated with a reduced risk for cardiovascular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and evaluation of nutritional factors with potential impact on haemostatic parameters and thrombotic risk.
the effects of nutritional factors on the haemorheologic system, especially the effects of a meditteranean diet.
the identification of the most important nutritional factors and the elucidation of the underlying mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nutrition has a strong influence on the haemorrhagic and thrombotic risk and that a balanced nutrition is a major factor in the prevention and therapy of cardiovascular and thrombotical diseases.
the mediterranean diet is the ideal diet in the prevention of thromboembolic diseases.
nutrition and lifestyle have a strong impact on the haematological system and that the mediterranean diet is a healthy diet with a variety of beneficial properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthy diet is a key element of a healthy life style and that a healthy life style has beneficial effects on cardiovascular health.
nutrition is a modifiable risk factor for thrombotic diseases and that the mediterranean diet is the most effective and safe nutritional approach to prevent cardiovascular disease.
the mediterranean diet is a healthy and balanced diet, which is characterized by a high intake of vegetables, fruit, whole grain, nuts, olive oil and fish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mediterranean diet, as a model of a healthy diet, is a promising strategy for primary prevention of atherosclerosis, thrombosis and cardiovascular diseases.
the haemostasis system is a highly sensitive target of dietary interventions.
a mediterranean dietary pattern is a powerful tool to reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases and to prevent thrombotic events.
